authoredPrompt: This figure is a single horizontal strip in which one camera is repeated five times in a row on a white ground, with thick red arrows between and around the copies. Each camera is a black wireframe viewing frustum in three-quarter view: a solid black dot marks the projection center at the left, four straight edges spread rightward from it to the corners of a tall rectangle standing for the image plane, and a faint vertical line inside that rectangle marks its midline. All five frusta match in size and orientation, and every one opens toward the right. A red arrow lies on the axis left of the first camera, another sits in each gap between consecutive cameras, and a final one continues past the last camera to the right edge; all arrowheads point right. Because the arrows run in the same direction the frusta face, the strip shows a camera moving straight ahead down its own optical axis, the case in which the sideways velocity components vanish and only the component along the Z-axis is nonzero.
authoredInteractions:
- Animation for advancing the camera copies along their optical axis; the frustum moves straight through the scene while projected points expand from the image center, linking forward Z translation to radial optical flow.
- Slider for time along the forward path; the active camera position and red direction arrows update together, showing that orientation stays fixed while depth to the scene changes.
- Toggle between the 3-D camera strip and the corresponding image-plane flow field; the visible update switches from rightward frustum motion to outward vectors, clarifying how forward translation becomes expansion in the image.
authoredContext:
For a camera moving forward, as illustrated in
the figure, note that $V_X = V_Y = 0$. In this
case, the motion is only along the $Z$-axis, $V_Z \neq 0$.

Camera moving forward, along the camera axis.
